name: Just For Men

lead: Just For Men is a consumer brand of dye for men's hair, moustaches and beards, designed to cover gray gradually or in one go. Covering gray is one way people try to look younger and more even in tone.
Results last until the hair grows out or the colour fades, so users repeat applications. As a category, home dyes range from temporary rinses to permanent products with developers.

paras: Users mix and apply a colour product to dry hair or beard, wait a set time, and rinse, usually following the product leaflet. Home dyes need re-application as roots and new gray hairs grow in.

Some hair dyes contain phenylenediamine (PPD), which can cause allergic reactions appearing hours to a day later; manufacturers generally recommend a patch test. Research on hair dye and cancer risk is described as limited and inconsistent.

chain: Dye deposits colour on gray strands
Hair and beard look darker and uniform
angle.text: The product covers gray in head hair and beards. The effect lasts until growth and washing fade it, so the look is maintained by repeat application.

lead: Just For Men is a brand of men's hair and beard colour used to cover gray. Grooming-minded men use dye to restore a darker, more uniform hair and beard colour, which many associate with looking younger.

As a product type, home hair dyes fall into permanent, demi-permanent, semi-permanent and temporary categories. Permanent dyes use developer and can lighten; semi-permanents wash out in a handful of shampoos and are better at blending a few gray hairs than covering a lot.[1]

Phenylenediamine-based dyes have drawn safety attention: allergic reactions can show up hours or a day later, and manufacturers often recommend a 48-hour patch test.[1] Reviews of hair dye and cancer link report limited and inconsistent evidence.[1]

paras: Permanent dyes contain ammonia and an oxidising developer that lifts natural pigment; demi-permanents use gentler alkaline agents and cannot lighten; semi-permanents rely on surface colour and last about 4 to 8 shampoos.[1] Demi-permanents cover gray better than semi-permanents but less well than permanents.[1]

Phenylenediamine dyes have been controversial and some products have been pulled from the market. Allergic reactions can include redness, itching and burning, and the EU restricts around 45 chemicals in hair dyes.[1] The IARC regards some hair dyes and ingredients as potentially mutagenic or carcinogenic, though the article reviewed describes the evidence linking hair dye use to cancers as limited and inconsistent.[1]
No studies found on the Just For Men brand specifically; studies of hair dye as a category are summarised under Safety.
